sources.title: Coverings of the Symmetric and Alternating Groups
sources.statement: An is the union of conjugates of two proper subgroups if and only if 4<=n<=8.
sources.application: Provides the lower bound of three classes for A10. The explicit H1,H3,W5 upper bound is proved here.
sources.reading_limits: Title, statement, hypotheses, and proof case architecture inspected through pdftotext. The full classification is imported, not independently reproved.

sources.title: Inertia groups and fibers
sources.locator: Theorem 0.2, page 2; setup and relation to Beckmann's Theorem 0.1, pages 1-3
sources.statement: For a generically Galois tamely ramified cover of curves over a global field, a fixed finite exceptional set suffices so specialization inertia outside it is trivial or conjugate to the relevant power subgroup of a geometric branch inertia group.
sources.application: Integral parameters avoid infinity outside an enlarged finite exceptional set. All nontrivial finite specialization inertia there is generated by a double transposition. Hensel roots handle every exceptional prime.
sources.reading_limits: Exact theorem, hypotheses, branch-intersection setup, and proof architecture inspected through pdftotext. Main specialization theorem and local-model proof are imported, not independently reproved.

sources.title: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem and the larger sieve
sources.locator: Section 1.1, Theorem 1.2 (Cohen, Serre), page 2; notation and full arithmetic-group specialization, pages 1-2
sources.statement: For the splitting field of a monic irreducible polynomial over k(T), exceptional integral one-parameter specializations over Q have count O(B^(1/2) log B); regularity is not required.
sources.application: Apply after affine substitution s=s_*+M0*n, whose generic group is still A10. Apply also to its compositum with any previously chosen finite Galois extension, whose generic group is A10 times the constant Galois group, to obtain linear disjointness.
sources.reading_limits: Exact integral statement and its preceding hypotheses inspected from retained primary paper. Cohen-Serre estimate is explicitly attributed and imported; no quantitative proof is claimed here.

sources.title: Two remarks on the inverse Galois problem for intersective polynomials
sources.version: Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 21 (2009), 435-437
sources.locator: Proposition and proof, printed page 436 (PDF page 3)
sources.statement: For nonsolvable G, ordinary inverse-Galois realizability over Q is equivalent to realizability by a nontrivially intersective polynomial. The proof uses the decomposition-group subgroup-cover criterion and solvability of local decomposition groups.
sources.application: Prevents claiming broad A10 Hasse/intersective existence as new. The local criterion used here is reproved directly; this source is not needed for the rank-301 construction's proof.
sources.reading_limits: Complete proposition and proof inspected through pdftotext, along with abstract and example context.

Complete 22 cycle types, all 945 perfect matchings, 2,880 even centralizer lifts for both local covers, exact counterexample, Hensel basepoint, component necessity and ranks; uniform partition sanity degrees 8 through 30.
Actual successful replay and checker hash.
Classification-backed exact seven maximal classes, four witness coset actions and complete weighted subset cover search.
Actual Sage10.9/GAP4.15.1/PrimGrp4.0.1 replay: minimum rank301 for full abstract DT local domain, minimum1075 with exactly three classes.

scope_limits: Three subgroup classes are sufficient and optimal in number for the entire abstract DT-inertia cyclic-quotient local domain.
Minimum total degrees 301 (any class count) and 1075 (exactly three classes) use the explicitly retained GAP/PrimGrp classification input.

Those minima concern coverage of all abstract local groups in the stated domain, not the minimum degree for an actual Hasse family with fewer ramification types. A rank-256 Hasse family remains possible if its actual decomposition groups fit H1,H3,W5.
The elementary checker covers the entire finite centralizer reduction, not the infinite arithmetic existence theorem. The second checker imports classified-library completeness.
The exceptional prime set and progression modulus are proved to exist; their numerical values and high-degree resolvent coefficients have not been computed.
Hasse algebras have A10 splitting fields, while their degree-301 Keller compiler maps have generic S301 by a separate retained theorem.
The finite-etale compiler is an existing theorem input, not independently reverified by this note.
One fixed three-dimensional map containing infinitely many of the complete rank-301 product fibres has not been proved here.
General intersective existence for nonsolvable realizable groups is already Sonn's result.
